body:
@sepo-agent /answer 

When the agent runs in orchestrator mode, it will start to gradually increase the scope or the original PR and it might start to incorporate some patch-y fixes rather than a good canonical design. I wonder should we consider adding a "self reflection step inside the orchestrator route such that it can rethink what happens in the implementation? See examples in: 


https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/158#issuecomment-4410485532

https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/166#issuecomment-4410324896

comments.body:
Yes. I would add it, but as a **structured reflection gate**, not just “ask the model to think harder.”

Current architecture already has an agent planner in `agent` mode: [`agent-orchestrator.yml`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/1dd7fdf1f27aae4944508926533b07dcd6924716/.github/workflows/agent-orchestrator.yml#L145-L186) runs the planner, then [`orchestrate-handoff.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/1dd7fdf1f27aae4944508926533b07dcd6924716/.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts#L1290-L1317) parses the result and dispatches. The runtime validates route transitions in [`handoff.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/1dd7fdf1f27aae4944508926533b07dcd6924716/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L469-L566), but it mostly asks “is this transition allowed?”, not “has the implementation drifted into patchy scope expansion?”

So the gap is real. In PR #158 and PR #166, the chain kept following concrete review findings, but some findings were actually architecture/scope signals. The orchestrator should pause and ask: “Is the next fix still the canonical implementation path, or are we now expanding the design enough that we should split, stop, or ask a human?”

Recommended approach:

1. Add a **Reflection Checkpoint** section to [`agent-orchestrator.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/1dd7fdf1f27aae4944508926533b07dcd6924716/.github/prompts/agent-orchestrator.md#L39-L98).
   It should require the planner to compare the original request, current PR/issue state, latest review findings, and accumulated handoff context.

2. Extend the planner JSON with structured fields like:
   - `scope_assessment`: `in_scope | bounded_extension | scope_creep | needs_split`
   - `design_assessment`: `canonical | patchy | uncertain`
   - `reflection_summary`
   - `split_recommendation`
   - `human_decision_required`

3. Update [`parsePlannerDecision`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/1dd7fdf1f27aae4944508926533b07dcd6924716/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L206-L263) and `decideAgentHandoff` so reflection is enforceable. For example: if `human_decision_required=true` or `scope_assessment=needs_split`, the runtime should stop/block visibly instead of dispatching another `fix-pr`.

4. Surface the reflection in stop comments from [`orchestrate-handoff.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/1dd7fdf1f27aae4944508926533b07dcd6924716/.agent/src/cli/orchestrate-handoff.ts#L1324-L1332), so the maintainer sees why the chain paused.

5. Add tests in `handoff.test.ts`, `orchestrate-handoff-cli.test.ts`, and `envelope.test.ts`, plus docs in [`agent-orchestrator.md`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/1dd7fdf1f27aae4944508926533b07dcd6924716/.agent/docs/technical-details/agent-orchestrator.md#L149-L169).

I would start with this integrated planner-gate version before adding a second LLM workflow step. It gives us most of the benefit with less runtime cost and less orchestration complexity. A separate `orchestrator-reflect` step can come later if the single planner still rubber-stamps patchy follow-ups.

Proposed implementation scope: add the structured checkpoint, enforce stop/block on scope drift, update visible comments/docs/tests. Please confirm whether to proceed with that scoped implementation.
Closing because this agent issue has had no activity for 30 days.

title: Add a self reflection step in orchestrator?
